name: Combination game
description: Scottish school of the late 19th century: the team moves together and passes the ball from foot to foot, against the English individual dribbling game.
phrase: I want the ball to move from foot to foot and the team to move together, not one player carrying it alone.

name: Danubian school
description: The passing game between the wars in Central Europe (Austria, Hungary, Czechoslovakia), with the game built collectively.
phrase: I want every pass and every movement to have a purpose, building the game with the ball on the ground.

name: WM (Chapman)
description: Chapman's formation at Arsenal after the offside change: three defenders, two half-backs and a five-man attack, with quick counter-attacks.
phrase: I want a team that gets results above all, defending with three centre-backs and attacking at speed.

name: Hungarian fluid 4-2-4
description: The Hungarian idea of the late 1940s and 1950s: a deep-lying centre-forward who organises the game and drags the centre-half out of position, with forwards interchanging.
phrase: I want a centre-forward who drops deep to organise the game and forwards who swap positions to unsettle the defence.

name: Futebol-arte / jogo bonito
description: Brazilian flair football in which individual talent comes first, against results-based football: beautiful play is the way to win.
phrase: I want the talent of the stars to lead the game, and believe that you can play well and win.

name: La Nuestra / Rioplatense
description: The Río de la Plata tradition of dribbling, short passing and improvisation by small, technical players, the criollo style the writers called 'la nuestra'.
phrase: I want a technical team, built on dribbling and short passing, with its own identity.

name: Total Football
description: Dutch school of the 1960s and 70s: everyone attacks and everyone defends, players swap positions, and the team presses high and occupies space collectively.
phrase: I want a team that presses high and where players swap positions, so that everyone attacks and everyone defends.

name: Catenaccio
description: Italian defensive system of the 1950s and 60s: a sweeper behind man-markers, a deep defence and quick counter-attacks, with results first.
phrase: I want to defend deep, with man-marking and a sweeper behind, and win on the counter-attack.

name: Gegenpressing
description: Counter-pressing right after losing the ball, developed in Germany by Rangnick, Klopp and others: win the ball back near the opponent's goal and attack before the defence sets up.
phrase: I want the team to press as soon as it loses the ball, to win it back near the opponent's goal and attack fast.

name: Soviet scientific football
description: Soviet school of Maslov and Lobanovskyi: systematic pressing, fitness and data analysis, with collective zonal play and the system above individuals.
phrase: I want a team that presses systematically, trains scientifically and plays in zones, with the system above individuals.

name: Cruyffism
description: Johan Cruyff's philosophy at Barcelona: attacking football, the ball as defence, positional play and youth development, with the team dominating the game.
phrase: I want a team that always attacks, uses the ball as its defence and is built from the academy, with positional play.

name: Tiki-taka
description: Popular name for the short-passing, patient possession football of Spain and Barcelona from 2008 to 2012; Guardiola rejected the term, and some treat it as another name for positional play.
phrase: I want a technical team that exchanges short passes and controls possession patiently.

name: Bielsismo
description: The style of Marcelo Bielsa and his followers such as Sampaoli: man-marking all over the pitch, high pressing, vertical attacks and very intense training.
phrase: I want man-marking all over the pitch, high pressing and vertical attacks, with very intense training.

name: Positional play
description: Game model in which the team occupies zones of the pitch with set spacing, seeks superiority between the lines and uses the third man; associated with Cruyff, Van Gaal, Lillo and Guardiola.
phrase: I want a team organised in zones, with set spacing and superiority between the lines, that controls possession.

name: Low block and counter-attack
description: An idea, not one team: absorb pressure in a compact deep block, give up possession and attack the space on the break with fast forwards; from Mourinho's Inter to Ranieri's Leicester.
phrase: I want a compact, deep team that lets the opponent have the ball and attacks the space on the counter.

name: Cholismo
description: Diego Simeone's style at Atlético Madrid: a deep, narrow 4-4-2, the collective above the individual, intensity and taking the game 'partido a partido' (one match at a time).
phrase: I want a deep, collective team that works harder than the opponent and takes one game at a time.

name: Mourinhismo
description: Result-first pragmatism: the plan and system change with the opponent and the squad, with a compact defence and counter-attacks; from Mourinho to Capello, Scolari and Deschamps.
phrase: I want a team that puts the result first and changes the plan according to the opponent and the squad.

name: Heavy metal football
description: High-energy football that began with Klopp and passed to the Red Bull school of Rangnick, Nagelsmann and Marsch: pressing and counter-pressing, maximum tempo and vertical transitions.
phrase: I want high-energy football with pressing, maximum tempo and quick attacks after winning the ball.

name: Relationism
description: An idea linked to Fernando Diniz and 'jogo funcional': position is a function of the relationships between players, with no zonal structure and the ball at the centre of the game.
phrase: I want a team without fixed positions, where players organise themselves through their relationships around the ball.

name: Player empowerment
description: Man-management football, as with Ancelotti, Zidane and Scaloni: light structure, rules on discipline and defending, and freedom with the ball built on trust.
phrase: I want few tactical rules, freedom with the ball and a coach who leads through trust in the players.

name: Vertical football
description: Win the ball, often through counter-pressing, and play it forward at once into space instead of building through midfield; tied to Klopp's Dortmund.
phrase: I want to win the ball and play it forward at once, running into space instead of building slowly.

name: Sarriball
description: Sarri's Napoli: a 4-3-3 of quick passing, one-two combinations, third-man runs and a high defensive line, at a vertical tempo.
phrase: I want quick passing and triangles, with a high defensive line and the team playing as a block.

name: Build-up baiting
description: De Zerbi's game: drawing the opponent's press during build-up from inside your own area, to create space and attack behind the pressing line.
phrase: I want to bait the opponent's press during build-up and, once they come, find the space behind it.

name: Modern man-to-man
description: Man-marking over much of the pitch, with an aggressive press and a back three, as in Gasperini's Atalanta.
phrase: I want to mark man to man over much of the pitch, with an aggressive press and a back three.

name: Zona mista
description: Trapattoni's gioco all'italiana: man-marking on the opposing playmaker or striker plus zonal cover, a sweeper, four defenders and quick transitions.
phrase: I want to man-mark the opposing star, cover the rest in zone and look for the result in quick transitions.
